comparison: Perfect agreement on HIV-AFMACS system development and validation (C1-C38). Both evaluations find the technical innovation compelling and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes experimental documentation while peer reviewers highlight innovation and use of primary cells as key strengths.

Significant disagreement on Vif target validation (C6, C79-C91). OpenEval finds comprehensive validation through multiple experimental approaches and considers claims well-supported. Peer reviewers accept the depletion data but express concern about 'limited validation' and 'unclear functional significance,' rating as UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on superior dataset quality compared to prior work (C100-C102). Both evaluations accept the quantitative comparison and acknowledge this as the largest primary CD4+ T cell dataset to date without challenge.

Agreement on AFMACS technical advantages (C92-C94). Both accept the methodological benefits, though peer reviewers note the discussion should be balanced with more thorough explanation of limitations.

Disagreement on adequacy of negative controls (C65-C68, C109). OpenEval finds controls demonstrate no artifactual changes and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2 raises critical concern that LNGFR overexpression and bead binding effects were not adequately evaluated, rating as UNCERTAIN.

Disagreement on VSVg pseudotyping limitation (C107-C108, C110). OpenEval finds the rationale sound and limitations appropriately acknowledged. Peer Reviewer 2 questions the experimental design choice, stating it was 'unfortunate' and suggesting wild-type Envelope would have been more compelling, rating as UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on identification of primary T cell-specific targets (C7-C8, C63-C64, C69-C71, C77-C78, C96-C97). Both evaluations accept the validation data and novelty of findings in primary cells, though peer reviewers note limited functional characterization.

Agreement on temporal proteomic profiling and validation (C40-C50, C72-C76). Both find the time course data technically sound and appropriately controlled. OpenEval emphasizes validation of known targets while peer reviewers find the approach compelling without specific concerns.

Agreement on dataset quality and resource value (C95-C97, C103-C106). Both evaluations praise the magnitude, depth, and accessibility of the data. Peer reviewers emphasize the interactive spreadsheet as an important community resource. OpenEval notes the 'first high coverage' claim should be qualified.

Agreement on reproducibility and pathway analysis (C5, C51-C59). Both evaluations accept the multi-donor findings and statistical thresholds without challenge. Peer reviewers note accessory protein effects as key observations of significant community interest.

Agreement on temporal pattern analysis distinguishing accessory protein mechanisms (C72-C76). Both find the mechanistic explanations supported by appropriate citations and consistent with HIV biology. Peer reviewers accept without specific concerns.

Agreement on lipid metabolism pathway findings (C60-C62). Both evaluations accept these observations as confirmatory of previous transcriptional studies. Peer reviewers treat as supporting rather than novel findings without challenge.

Agreement on comprehensive proteomic data quality (C3-C4, C39). Both evaluations praise the quantitation of ~9000 proteins and technical rigor. Peer reviewers emphasize depth and stringency while OpenEval highlights validation of known targets.

Agreement on Vpr substrate validation (C78). Both accept ARID5B as a known Vpr target used for comparison. Peer Reviewer 1 notes overlap with parallel work (Greenwood 2018) but validation in primary cells is not challenged.

Agreement on interpretation of direct vs indirect effects (C112). Both evaluations accept the distinction between downregulated and upregulated changes. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this framework without challenge.

OpenEval finds background and rationale claims (C9-C18) well-supported by cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific background claims, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the rationale by praising the emphasis on primary cells.

OpenEval finds interpretive synthesis (C111-C115) supported, noting mechanistic explanations for upregulated proteins remain somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation directly addresses these interpretive claims.

OpenEval finds functional context claims (C116-C121) supported with appropriate citations, emphasizing discovery aspect. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific functional context claims.
OpenEval finds explanations for discrepancies with prior literature (C98-C99) reasonable and well-supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation directly addresses these reconciliation claims.
